name: Lule Saami
variety: Lule Saami as written in the 1983 standard orthography and spoken around Jokkmokk (Sweden) and Tysfjord/Divtasvuodna (Norway)
sources: Spiik, Nils Eric (1989). Lulesamisk grammatik. Jokkmokk: Sameskolstyrelsen.
Sammallahti, Pekka (1998). The Saami Languages: An Introduction. Kárášjohka: Davvi Girji.
Ylikoski, Jussi (2022). Lule Saami. In Bakró-Nagy, Marianne; Laakso, Johanna; Skribnik, Elena (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Uralic Languages. Oxford University Press.

Fangel-Gustavson, Nora; Ridouane, Rachid; Morén-Duolljá, Bruce (2014). Quantity contrast in Lule Saami: a three-way system. Proceedings of the 10th International Seminar on Speech Production (ISSP), Cologne.
Wiklund, K. B. (1891). Laut- und Formenlehre der Lule-lappischen Dialekte.
contrasts: three degrees of consonant quantity after a stressed vowel (Q1 short, Q2 long, Q3 overlong), alternating in consonant gradation
vowel length (short against long) and four diphthongs
preaspirated stops and affricates (hp, ht, hk, hts, htj) against plain ones
pre-stopped nasals (bm, dn, dnj, gŋ) against plain nasals
palatal /ɲ ʎ ɟ/ against alveolars and velars
allophony: the stops written b, d, g are voiceless unaspirated at the beginning of a word; voiced stops and affricates proper occur only in quantity 3 (the palatal /ɟ/ also in quantity 2)
the stops written p, t, k are aspirated at the beginning of a stressed syllable
the stop of a pre-stopped nasal is unreleased
/v/ is a labiodental fricative [v] in a syllable onset and a bilabial glide [w] in a syllable coda
/ea̯/ is a diphthong or a long monophthong [ɛː]
diphthong simplification: /ea̯ oɑ̯/ become /eː oː/ when the next syllable has a short vowel and the consonant between is in quantity 1 or 2
a short vowel in the second syllable is lengthened after a stressed short vowel followed by a quantity 1 consonant
unstressed /a aː/ are rounded to /o oː/ after a stressed short /o/
quantity 3 clusters of a sonorant and another consonant are broken by a short epenthetic vowel

in quantity 3 the first part of a geminate or cluster is lengthened; consonant duration rises step by step from Q1 to Q2 to Q3, with slight adjustment of the following vowel (Fangel-Gustavson et al. 2014)
phonotactics: long /eː/ and the diphthongs /ea̯ oɑ̯/ occur only in stressed syllables; long /iː uː/ and short /e/ are rare
short /o/ and long /oː/ occur in unstressed syllables only after a stressed /o/
single /h/ and /j/ occur only in quantity 1; /ʎ/ only in quantities 2 and 3
the spelling writes quantity 2 and quantity 3 geminates alike (both double)
initial consonant clusters occur mainly in Scandinavian loanwords

stress.rule: Primary stress falls on the first syllable, with secondary stress on later odd-numbered syllables that are not word-final, so that words divide into two-syllable feet.
stress.cues: duration patterns within the foot (vowel length and consonant quantity) and the fuller vowel inventory of stressed syllables; no instrumental study of pitch or intensity was found

rhythm.vowel_reduction: moderate: unstressed syllables have a smaller vowel set, but the vowels are not reduced to schwa
rhythm.notes: Timing is built on the two-syllable foot and its quantity pattern, as in other Saami languages. No rhythm metrics have been published.

length.notes: Consonants and clusters after a stressed vowel come in three quantities. An acoustic study of seven speakers from Tysfjord found a large and regular rise in consonant duration from Q1 to Q2 to Q3, with smaller compensating changes in the neighbouring vowels and in vowel intensity (Fangel-Gustavson et al. 2014). No durations are given here because the figures could not be checked.

intonation.declarative: not described in the sources consulted; a falling contour is assumed
intonation.yes_no_question: not described in the sources consulted; questions are marked by word order and by the question particle
intonation.wh_question: not described in the sources consulted
intonation.continuation: not described in the sources consulted
intonation.accent_shape: not described in the sources consulted
intonation.notes: No study of Lule Saami intonation was found. These fields should be treated as open.

phonation: preaspiration of stops and affricates after a stressed vowel
aspiration of p, t, k at the start of a stressed syllable

problems: the voice is marked 'status testing' and its phoneme table is a copy of the Finnish one with a few additions; it keeps the eighteen Finnish diphthong phonemes, of which only ie and uo belong to Lule Saami
quantity 3 is not told apart from quantity 2 in geminates (the spelling writes both double), so bállo and similar forms get one long consonant of fixed length
preaspiration is deleted in the quantity 3 spellings hkk, hpp, htt (áhkko is given as [ɑːkːuo]); descriptions have the first element lengthened there, not dropped
nj is rendered as [n], a short pause and [j] instead of the palatal nasal [ɲ], and lj has no rule, so [ʎ] is missing
the letter i is always long [iː] (idja, loddi), although long /iː/ is rare in the language
v in a syllable coda stays [v] (biejvve, jávrre) instead of the glide [w]
the epenthetic vowel of quantity 3 clusters is produced only for a fixed list of vowel and cluster spellings
no aspiration of p, t, k in native words (only before á in loanword rules)
intonation uses the generic flat tune set (group 3); nothing is language-specific
good: word-initial b, d, g are voiceless and become voiced between vowels
second-syllable vowel lengthening after a short first syllable is attempted in the rules
unstressed e and o are given as diphthongs [ie] and [uo], as in the orthographic description
a word list of about 2,900 entries covers numbers, ordinals and unstressed function words (postpositions, pronouns)

notes: Published phonetic work on Lule Saami is small. The inventory follows the descriptions based on Spiik (1989); vowel formants, VOT and rhythm measures are left out because no figures were found that could be checked.
